transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-09
Start: 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Jules Carver (Tidal Head of ML), Priya Nair (Tidal Platform Eng), Marcus Lee (Tidal Procurement)

Summary: quick checkin to lock down renewal timing, discuss capacity bump and EU region, and get agreement on next technical steps for benchmark.

[00:00:05] Samira: Hey everyone, good to see you - thanks for making time today, we'll keep to ~30 minutes, want to run through renewal options and the expansion ask from Jules.
[00:00:18] Jules: Yep thanks, Samira. We are happy with Redwood in general, latency's been solid in US, but we're expecting a big EU launch Q4 so need more dedicated capacity and lower EU tail latency.
[00:00:30] Diego: Got it - congrats on the launch. Quick clarifying q: when you say dedicated capacity, do you mean reserved GPU pools or dedicated nodes in a private deployment?
[00:00:42] Jules: Reserved pools yeah. We like the hosted model but want isolation and predictability. Also thinking about burst for peak trading hours.
[00:00:54] Priya: And we'd want the EU region to be run by Redwood's EU infra, not via cross-region egress - compliance is picky.
[00:01:06] Samira: Totally - we can quote reserved capacity in EU and set up burst policies. For renewal length we can do pricing tiers at 12/24/36 months with escalating discounts. Marcus, are you able to talk timelines on procurement?
[00:01:20] Marcus: Yep procurement is targetting signing by end of August if pricing lines up. If we pick 36 months we need legal to review a week earlier, but we can move fast.
[00:01:32] Diego: On the technical side, we'll need to run a 95th-percentile latency benchmark in EU with your staging traffic. We can spin up a temporary EU pool and run the traces. Note: there may be small diffs because KV cache warmup is regional.
[00:01:48] Jules: When you say KV cache, do you mean the KV cash? - sorry, cribbing, I heard that wrong earlier.
[00:01:54] Diego: Yeah KV cache - key-value cache for prompt prefixes. Important for tail lat.
[00:02:05] Priya: For security - we need SOC 2 docs, SAML SSO integration, and confirmation KMS is customer-managed for keys in EU.
[00:02:16] Samira: We have a SOC 2 pack and SAML flows; KMS customer-managed is supported in our Private/VPC options. For hosted EU we can offer KMS integration with customer keys - I'll attach the security pack.
[00:02:30] Jules: Great. About cost: rough ask is 3x our current reserved capacity. Can you confirm lead time to provision and the monthly delta?
[00:02:42] Samira: Provisioning lead time is typically 7-10 business days for reserved pools in a new region. Pricing delta I'll calculate - the big levers are reserved commit size and term length. For 36-month commit we'd be able to give the highest discount and include some burst credits for peaks.
[00:03:00] Marcus: If you can include credit for initial burst and a price cap for the first 12 months that'd help finance sign-off.
[00:03:08] Samira: We can propose a burst allowance and a 12-month price cap in the quote.
[00:03:15] Diego: On performance, two notes - 1) we recommend using Redwood Dedicated in EU for predictable p99 latency and 2) enable prefix caching + batching policies, which vary per model. We can share a recommended config for your workload.
[00:03:31] Jules: Do you have a sense of differences between Dedicated vs Private for our case? We prefer hosted but want data controls.
[00:03:38] Diego: Dedicated is still hosted but with reserved GPU pools and isolated tenants; Private gives you full VPC control and customer-managed control plane if you need air-gap or strict residency. For most teams Dedicated is simpler and meets SOC2 + KMS requirements.
[00:03:55] Priya: Interesting - if Dedicated meets KMS in EU then it's preferable. Private adds ops overhead.
[00:04:03] Marcus: From procurement POV, contract language around data residency and audit logs is crucial.
[00:04:10] Samira: Understood - we'll include language about audit logs, retention, and region-specific processing in the SOW.
[00:04:20] Jules: On benchmarks - Diego, can you run a bench with our staging traffic shape? We have a spike pattern around 14:00-15:00 UTC that caused oom in our prior setup.
[00:04:31] Diego: Yes, we can schedule that. Ideally send a short sample traffic trace and we'll mimic the prefix lengths. We'll also run a KV cache warmup to show steady-state p95/p99 numbers.
[00:04:45] Priya: We'll send the trace and the growth forecast - expect roughly 2.5x baseline by Q4.
[00:04:53] Samira: Perfect. I'll include an option in the quote: 3x reserved commit in EU + US, 36-month term with burst credits and a 12-month price cap.
[00:05:05] Marcus: That sounds reasonable, if legal signs off I'm optimistic.
[00:05:12] Jules: One more question - what's the rollback or fallback if Redwood EU has a partial outage?
[00:05:18] Diego: We can set policy-based routing: failover to US with added latency but we can also pre-provision a warm standby in another region - that costs more but improves RTO. We'll outline options in the SOW.
[00:05:33] Priya: Also need clarity on data egress charges between regions.
[00:05:38] Samira: We'll include egress estimates.
[00:05:42] [Longer silence as people check notes]
[00:06:10] Samira: Okay recap - next steps: I'll send updated quote by Friday 8/12 that includes EU pricing, 3x reserved capacity, 36-month and 24/12 term options, burst credits and 12-month price cap. Diego will run the EU benchmark and share logs by 8/16 once Priya shares traffic traces. Priya to share traffic matrix by 8/11. Marcus will confirm procurement timeline.
[00:06:34] Marcus: We'll aim to turn docs around quickly.
[00:06:40] Jules: Appreciate it. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[00:06:44] Diego: No blockers; we may need a short SE access window to their staging for traffic replay.
[00:06:50] Priya: We'll set that up.
[00:06:55] Samira: Great - I'll also attach SOC 2 pack and the SAML integration guide.
[00:07:02] Jules: Thanks.

[00:07:20] - brief technical sidebar about model quantization and cost -
[00:07:22] Diego: Quick note, depending on the model we can recommend a quantization profile to reduce cost without impacting quality. We'll include suggestions for batch sizes and tokenization settings in the benchmark report.
[00:07:35] Jules: Good - cost is important.

[00:08:00] [Wrap up and confirmations]
[00:08:05] Samira: I'll send the quote + security docs. Diego will follow up re: bench schedule. Priya will send the traffic. Marcus will start legal loop. Any final q's?
[00:08:16] Jules: None from me, thanks.
[00:08:19] Marcus: All good.
[00:08:22] Priya: All set.
[00:08:25] Samira: Thank you everyone - we'll be in touch and aim to get these items done ahead of your target.

Notes about transcription: some words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache"), but context preserved. Links referenced: quote template (link to internal drive), SOC2 pack (link), SAML integration doc (link).

Final recap (verbatim):
- Samira: send updated quote for 3x reserved in EU/US, 36/24/12 term options, 12-month price cap, burst credits (due 2027-08-12)
- Diego: schedule and run EU region benchmark + share logs (due 2027-08-16)
- Priya: share traffic matrix and compliance contact (due 2027-08-11)

End of transcript.
